description: Consolidated system health: HTTP, DB, WS, runtime + Postgres internals, query performance. Progressive disclosure via collapsed rows.

panels.description: Normal: < 500ms p95 (green). Watch for: sustained yellow (> 500ms) or red (> 1s). Check next: Lifecycle Timing in Orient for breakdown.
panels.title: HTTP Latency p95

panels.description: Normal: < 50ms p95 (green). Watch for: yellow (> 50ms) signals pool pressure, red (> 100ms) signals contention. Check next: Database collapsed row in Orient.
panels.title: DB Transaction p95

panels.description: Normal: < 1% errors (green). Watch for: yellow (> 1%) may be transient; red (> 5%) indicates systematic failures. Check next: HTTP Error Rate timeseries in Server & HTTP.
panels.title: HTTP Error Rate %

panels.description: Normal: < 60% utilization (green). Watch for: yellow (> 60%) under moderate load, red (> 80%) approaching saturation. Check next: Pool Usage timeseries in Database collapsed row.
panels.title: Pool Utilization

panels.description: Normal: 0 canceled acquires (green). Watch for: any non-zero rate (red) means requests timing out waiting for DB connections. Check next: Pool Utilization and Acquire Time in Database row.
panels.title: Canceled Acquires

panels.description: Normal: > 99% cache hit rate (green). Watch for: yellow (< 99%) indicates working set exceeds shared_buffers; red (< 90%) severe miss rate. Check next: Postgres Internals collapsed row.
panels.title: Cache Hit Rate

panels.description: Normal: < 100 connections (green). Watch for: yellow (> 100) under moderate load; red (> 500) may indicate leak. Check next: WebSocket collapsed row for broadcast health.
panels.title: WS Connections

panels.description: Normal: HTTP Total < 500ms, DB < 50ms, Game Logic < 200ms, WS < 100ms. Watch for: any boundary diverging from baseline. Check next: collapsed rows below for per-boundary detail.
panels.title: Lifecycle Timing (p95)

panels.description: Normal: tight bands (p50-p95 close together). Watch for: p99 band widening (tail latency divergence). Check next: Server & HTTP collapsed row for per-route breakdown.
panels.title: HTTP Latency Percentile Bands

panels.description: Normal: both isolation levels < 50ms p95. Watch for: repeatable read diverging from read committed (serialization retries). Check next: Database collapsed row for pool pressure.
panels.title: Isolation Rhythm

panels.description: Normal: all handlers < 100ms p95. Watch for: individual handlers exceeding 200ms (slow consumer). Check next: Event Bus collapsed row for throughput.
panels.title: Handler Performance

panels.description: Normal: p95 < 50ms, p99 < 100ms. Watch for: p99 diverging from p95 (long-tail transactions). Check next: Pool Usage for saturation.
panels.title: Txn Duration P50/P95/P99

panels.description: Normal: active well below total, healthy idle buffer. Watch for: active approaching total (saturation). Check next: Acquire Time for queue pressure.
panels.title: Pool Usage

panels.description: Normal: < 1ms average acquire time. Watch for: sustained > 10ms (pool exhaustion starting). Check next: Canceled Acquires in Observe.
panels.title: Acquire Time (avg)

panels.description: Normal: < 60% with SLO line visible. Watch for: crossing yellow threshold under normal load. Check next: Acquire Rate for demand side.
panels.title: Pool Saturation

panels.description: Normal: proportional to request rate. Watch for: spikes not correlated with traffic. Check next: Rollbacks for failed transactions.
panels.title: Acquire Rate

panels.description: Normal: near zero rollback rate. Watch for: sustained rollbacks indicating transaction conflicts. Check next: PG Connections for connection-level issues.
panels.title: Rollbacks

panels.description: Normal: stable connection count matching pool size. Watch for: gradual increase (connection leak). Check next: PG Txns/sec for throughput.
panels.title: PG Connections

panels.description: Normal: commits >> rollbacks. Watch for: rollback rate approaching commit rate. Check next: PG Rows for row-level throughput.
panels.title: PG Txns/sec

panels.description: Normal: returned/fetched dominate (read-heavy workload). Watch for: updated/inserted spikes not correlated with game activity. Check next: Postgres Internals in Decide.
panels.title: PG Rows

panels.description: Normal: rate proportional to move rate (each move triggers multiple handlers). Watch for: rate dropping to zero while games are active. Check next: Handler Latency for slow consumers.
panels.title: Handler Throughput

panels.description: Normal: all handlers < 100ms p95. Watch for: individual handlers diverging (slow snapshot fetch or WS broadcast). Check next: Handler Performance bar gauge in Orient.
panels.title: Handler Latency P95

panels.description: Normal: AccessShareLock dominates (read-heavy workload). Watch for: ExclusiveLock or RowExclusiveLock spikes (write contention). Check next: Postgres Internals in Decide for full lock breakdown.
panels.title: Lock Activity

panels.description: Normal: low dead tuple count (autovacuum keeping up). Watch for: monotonic growth on any table (vacuum falling behind). Check next: Postgres Internals in Decide for table scans.
panels.title: Dead Tuples

panels.description: Normal: > 99% per table. Watch for: individual tables dropping below 95% (hot table exceeding buffer cache). Check next: Per-Table Cache Hit in Postgres Internals for trend.
panels.title: Cache Efficiency

panels.description: Normal: stable request rate matching expected load. Watch for: sudden drops (upstream issue) or spikes (load surge). Check next: HTTP Error Rate % for failure ratio.
panels.title: HTTP Request Rate

panels.description: Normal: < 1% with SLO line visible. Watch for: error rate crossing SLO threshold. Check next: HTTP Latency P50/P95/P99 for latency correlation.
panels.title: HTTP Error Rate %

panels.description: Normal: p50 < 100ms, p95 < 500ms, p99 < 1s. Watch for: p99 diverging sharply from p95 (long tail). Check next: HTTP Rate by Route for per-endpoint breakdown.
panels.title: HTTP Latency P50/P95/P99

panels.description: Normal: move endpoints dominate. Watch for: unusual routes or disproportionate rates. Check next: Game Engine dashboard for game-specific routes.
panels.title: HTTP Rate by Route

panels.description: Normal: < 1 core under normal load. Watch for: sustained increase correlated with game count. Check next: Scheduler Latency for GC pressure.
panels.title: Process CPU

panels.description: Normal: < 1ms scheduler latency. Watch for: spikes during GC pauses or high goroutine count. Check next: Goroutines for concurrency.
panels.title: Scheduler Latency

panels.description: Normal: stable count proportional to active games. Watch for: monotonic increase (goroutine leak). Check next: Heap Memory for memory pressure.
panels.title: Goroutines

panels.description: Normal: heap alloc tracks used with sawtooth GC pattern. Watch for: used growing without release (heap pressure). Check next: GC Goal for tuning.
panels.title: Heap Memory

panels.description: Normal: GOGC at 100%, GOMEMLIMIT stable or absent. Watch for: GOMEMLIMIT being approached by heap usage (OOM risk). Check next: Runtime Memory for total footprint.
panels.title: GC Goal

panels.description: Normal: stable memory proportional to heap + stack. Watch for: monotonic growth (memory leak). Check next: Goroutines for stack memory contributors.
panels.title: Runtime Memory

panels.description: Normal: p95 < 100ms. Watch for: p99 > 500ms (slow consumers blocking broadcast). Check next: Messages Rate for throughput.
panels.title: Broadcast Latency P50/P95/P99

panels.description: Normal: steady rate proportional to active games. Watch for: rate dropping to zero while games are active. Check next: Fan-Out for amplification ratio.
panels.title: Messages Rate

panels.description: Normal: ~4 (one message per connected player per broadcast). Watch for: 0 (no connected players). Check next: WS Connections.
panels.title: Fan-Out

panels.description: Normal: 0 errors. Watch for: any sustained error rate (broken connections, write failures). Check next: WS Connections in Observe for connection count.
panels.title: WS Errors

panels.description: Normal: ~4x (one per player). Watch for: > 10x (SLO yellow) suggests broadcast storms. Check next: WebSocket collapsed row for per-message detail.
panels.title: Fan-out Amplification

panels.description: Normal: 30-50% (DB is a fraction of total latency). Watch for: > 70% (SLO yellow) means DB dominates request time. Check next: Postgres Internals collapsed row.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_name="risk-it", span_name=~"db[.]transaction"}[1m])) by (le)) / histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_name="risk-it", span_name=~"(GET|POST|PUT|DELETE) .*"}[1m])) by (le)) * 100

panels.title: DB Latency Share

panels.description: Normal: used memory tracks heap alloc with stable overhead. Watch for: used growing without GC reclaiming (heap leak). Check next: Goroutines in Server & HTTP row.
panels.title: Runtime Memory

panels.description: Normal: AccessShareLock dominates (read locks, green). Watch for: ExclusiveLock or AccessExclusiveLock spikes (red/orange — DDL or heavy writes). Check next: Deadlocks for escalated contention.
panels.title: Lock Contention

panels.description: Normal: 0 deadlocks. Watch for: any non-zero rate indicates transaction ordering issues. Check next: Lock Contention for lock type breakdown.
panels.title: Deadlocks

panels.description: Normal: low dead tuple count (autovacuum keeping up). Watch for: monotonic growth on any table (vacuum falling behind). Check next: Table Scans for sequential scan impact.
panels.title: Dead Tuples

panels.description: Normal: idx scans >> seq scans. Watch for: seq scan rate (dashed) approaching idx scan rate (missing index). Check next: Live Tuples for table growth.
panels.title: Table Scans

panels.description: Normal: stable row counts proportional to game count. Watch for: rapid growth on single table (data accumulation). Check next: WAL for write amplification.
panels.title: Live Tuples

panels.description: Normal: stable WAL size within configured retention. Watch for: WAL size growing unbounded (archiving or replication lag). Check next: Per-Table Cache Hit for buffer efficiency.
panels.title: WAL Size

panels.description: Normal: > 99% per table. Watch for: individual tables dropping below 95% (hot table exceeding cache). Check next: Live Tuples for growth correlation.
panels.title: Per-Table Cache Hit

panels.description: Normal: dense band at low latencies (< 10ms). Watch for: heat spreading to higher buckets over time. Check next: Postgres Internals for lock and vacuum state.
panels.title: Query Latency Heatmap

panels.description: Normal: few or no traces > 250ms. Watch for: recurring slow traces on same endpoint. Check next: click Trace ID to load waterfall below.
panels.title: Slow Traces (> 250ms)

panels.description: Normal: broadcast log entries for each move. Watch for: error-level entries or timeouts. Check next: Trace Investigation collapsed row for correlated traces.
panels.title: WS Broadcast Logs

panels.description: Normal: event stream showing game lifecycle (moves, phase transitions, completions). Watch for: gaps in event flow or unexpected event types. Check next: Event Bus collapsed row in Orient for handler performance.
panels.title: Game Event Logs

panels.description: Normal: complete span tree visible. Watch for: missing spans (instrumentation gaps) or long gaps between spans (async contention). Check next: Correlated Logs below.
panels.title: Trace Waterfall

panels.description: Normal: log lines matching the traced request. Watch for: error-level entries or unexpected log patterns. Check next: return to Observe tiles for current system state.
panels.title: Correlated Logs

title: System Health
